headline: Five things moved since the August 31 briefing. Everything else on the register is unchanged and is listed at the foot without being repeated.
scope: Built from the public record alone: filings accepted by EDGAR, press releases, and the company's own pages, read on September 15, 2026. No internal source of any kind.

items.headline: The window to nominate a director for the 2026 annual meeting shut on Sunday, and the meeting date is still not public

chain.label: WHAT HAPPENED
chain.text: The bylaw window for stockholder proposals and director nominations at the 2026 annual meeting closed at the close of business on Sunday, September 13, 2026. It had opened on August 14.

sources.title: Definitive proxy statement (DEF 14A) for the December 12, 2025 annual meeting
sources.quote: any stockholder who would like to have a proposal considered at our 2026 annual meeting of stockholders must submit the proposal to the Secretary of the Company at the Company's principal executive offices so that it is received by not earlier than the close of business on August 14, 2026, and not later than the close of business on September 13, 2026

chain.label: WHAT CHANGED
chain.text: On August 31 this was an open window with thirteen days to run. It is now shut. Nothing has been filed since to announce the date of the meeting.

sources.title: Definitive proxy statement (DEF 14A) for the December 12, 2025 annual meeting
sources.quote: any stockholder who would like to have a proposal considered at our 2026 annual meeting of stockholders must submit the proposal to the Secretary of the Company at the Company's principal executive offices so that it is received by not earlier than the close of business on August 14, 2026, and not later than the close of business on September 13, 2026

sources.title: Definitive proxy statement (DEF 14A) for the December 12, 2025 annual meeting
sources.quote: unless the date of our 2026 annual meeting is more than 30 days before or more than 60 days after December 12, 2026, in which case the proposal must be received no later than the 10th day following the day on which public announcement of the date of such meeting is first made by the Company

chain.label: WHY IT MATTERS
chain.text: The same paragraph reopens the window for ten days after a public announcement if the 2026 meeting falls more than 30 days before, or more than 60 days after, December 12, 2026. Setting the meeting date therefore decides whether the window stays shut or opens again. Reading it the other way round: as long as the date is unset, the answer to whether nominations are closed is unsettled. Whether a submission received on Monday, September 14 would be treated as timely against a Sunday deadline is a question for counsel, not for this briefing.

items.headline: Seven amended insider reports were filed in thirteen minutes on September 8, one of them correcting a report from March 2024
answers: WHAT CHANGED IN THE LAST 24 HOURS

chain.label: WHAT HAPPENED
chain.text: EDGAR indexes seven Forms 4/A under the filing date September 8, 2026, accepted between 21:02 and 21:15 Eastern. They amend reports for five insiders. One of them corrects a report originally filed on March 18, 2024.

sources.title: EDGAR index of the company's Section 16 ownership reports
Form 4/A for director Bob McFarland amending a report originally filed March 18, 2024
sources.quote: 4. If Amendment, Date of Original Filed (Month/Day/Year) 03/18/2024

chain.label: WHAT CHANGED
chain.text: None of this existed at the August 31 briefing. One of the amended reports is itself only a week old: the Form 4 filed on September 1, 2026 carries a date of earliest transaction of December 13, 2024 while the transaction it reports is an award of 2,150 shares dated September 1, 2026. The amendment filed seven days later restates that date as September 1, 2026.

sources.title: Form 4 for director Charles Arch Winn, filed September 1, 2026
sources.quote: 3. Date of Earliest Transaction (Month/Day/Year) 12/13/2024

sources.title: Form 4 for director Charles Arch Winn, filed September 1, 2026
sources.quote: Common Stock 09/01/2026 A 2,150

sources.title: Form 4/A amending that report, filed September 8, 2026
sources.quote: 3. Date of Earliest Transaction (Month/Day/Year) 09/01/2026

chain.label: WHY IT MATTERS
chain.text: A batch that reaches across five insiders and back to a report from March 2024 reads as the output of a review of past filings rather than a single clerical fix. This briefing can see the output on EDGAR and not the review itself, so that reading is offered as a reading. What is not a reading is the calendar: the proxy statement has to name every insider whose Section 16(a) report was late during the fiscal year, and last year's named three people by name and date.

items.headline: Your public record disagrees with itself about the size of your board, in three places
answers: WHAT SHOULD I KNOW THAT NOBODY HAS DIRECTLY TOLD ME
items.new_since_previous: the company's own board page was read on September 15 and still shows six directors, sixty one days after the seventh was appointed

chain.label: WHAT HAPPENED
chain.text: Item 5.02 of the Form 8-K of July 22, 2026 says the Board went from six directors to seven and appointed Matthew Kreps. The press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to that same filing says it went from five to six. The Executive Team page on the company site presents the Chairman and five directors, six names, and no seventh.

sources.title: Form 8-K, Item 5.02: appointment of a seventh director
sources.quote: increased the size of the Board from six directors to seven directors and appointed Matthew Kreps to the Board to serve as a director until the Company's 2026 annual meeting of stockholders

sources.title: Press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to the July 22, 2026 Form 8-K
sources.quote: it has increased the size of its Board of Directors from five to six directors and has appointed Matt Kreps as a director of the Company

sources.title: Executive Team and Board Members page on astrotechcorp.com
sources.quote: Thomas B. Pickens, III Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board [...] Board Members [...] Tom Wilkinson Lead Independent Director [...] Bob McFarland Director [...] John Halinski Director [...] Eric Stober Director [...] Charles Winn Director

chain.label: WHAT CHANGED
chain.text: The contradiction inside the July 22 filing was in the August 31 briefing. What is new is the reconciliation: the board page was read on September 15, sixty one days after the July 16 board action, and has not caught up. The same page lists a Chief Operating Officer and a Chief Product Officer and no Chief Financial Officer, while an Interim Chief Financial Officer, Treasurer and Secretary has been in office since October 27, 2025.

sources.title: Executive Team and Board Members page on astrotechcorp.com
sources.quote: Thomas B. Pickens, III Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board [...] Board Members [...] Tom Wilkinson Lead Independent Director [...] Bob McFarland Director [...] John Halinski Director [...] Eric Stober Director [...] Charles Winn Director

sources.title: Executive Team and Board Members page on astrotechcorp.com
sources.quote: Nihanth Badugu is the Chief Operating Officer of Astrotech Corporation [...] As Chief Product Officer at Astrotech Corporation

sources.title: Form 8-K, Item 5.02: appointment of an Interim Chief Financial Officer
sources.quote: On October 27, 2025, the Board of Directors of Astrotech Corporation (the "Company") appointed Scott Bartley, as Interim Chief Financial Officer, Treasurer and Secretary of the Company

chain.label: WHY IT MATTERS
chain.text: Six directors stood for election on December 12, 2025, so six plus one is seven and the Item 5.02 figure is the one that agrees with the record. The press release is the document that travels: data vendors and proxy advisers read it first, and the website is what a counterparty checks second. The 2026 proxy statement will have to state one number, in writing, with seven names under it.
